key_insight: Estimating the watermarked share of an edited corpus requires explicit editing constraints; without them, the share’s upper bound is 100%.
engineering_relevance: Corpus auditors can use finite-sample bounds and streaming confidence sequences, but must account for editing assumptions and detector-null calibration.
method: Derive power envelopes for Gumbel-max and KGW watermarks using retention, entropy and substitution budgets.
Convert envelopes into prevalence bounds using an exact null or an independent human calibration sample.
Extend inference to confidence sequences for document streams.
evidence_signal: Tests on OPT-1.3B and Qwen3-1.7B text included 12,000 fresh human documents scored under three keys; all reported finite-pool resampling bounds covered, with an exact-null interval around [0.14, 0.38] at a true share of 0.20.
watch_item: Paraphrasing can violate the envelope, and a simulated null error of 0.01 broke exact-null coverage at 100,000 documents; independent calibration preserved coverage but required a large reference sample for narrow bounds.
paper_title: Prevalence Bounds for Edited Watermarked Text: Power Envelopes and Calibration Sensitivity
